svg.title: Medallion Lakehouse on Microsoft Fabric: Bronze, Silver, Gold on One OneLake
svg.desc: An architectural infographic tracing data from external ingestion routes into Bronze raw Delta landing in OneLake, through Spark cleansing and conforming to Silver, Spark aggregation into Gold star schemas, and dual read-only serving via SQL Analytics Endpoint and Direct Lake for Power BI, backed by a Delta transaction log and multi-layer security.
svg.text: Medallion Lakehouse Architecture on Microsoft Fabric
Bronze, Silver & Gold in One OneLake · Multi-engine processing with zero data duplication · Direct Lake and T-SQL serving

g.title: Source ingestion (pipeline / Dataflow / shortcut) — Data enters the lakehouse through pipeline copy, Dataflow Gen2, Spark jobs, or OneLake shortcuts.
Bronze: raw Delta landing (Tables area) — Raw data auto-registers as a Delta table in the lakehouse's managed Tables area.
Spark: cleanse & conform to silver — Spark de-duplicates, types, and joins bronze into validated, query-ready silver Delta tables.
Spark: aggregate to gold — Spark aggregates silver into curated, business-ready gold Delta tables.

svg.text: Single source of truth via commit JSONs · Optimistic concurrency · Checkpoint every 10 commits
Zero data movement between Bronze, Silver, and Gold — all metadata-tracked commits inside OneLake

g.title: SQL analytics endpoint (read-only T-SQL) — Auto-provisioned at lakehouse creation; exposes gold Delta tables to read-only T-SQL.
Direct Lake (Power BI semantic model) — Power BI reads gold Delta files straight from OneLake, lazily, with no import or refresh.
g.text: Sub-second visuals over billions of rows

g.aria-label: Trap: endpoint permissions don't cover Spark/OneLake reads
g.title: Trap: endpoint permissions don't cover Spark/OneLake reads — SQL-endpoint GRANT/DENY only applies through that endpoint; Spark and OneLake reads bypass it.
g.text: SQL Endpoint GRANT/DENY Does NOT Secure Spark or OneLake Direct Reads
The Failure Mode (Securing Only SQL Path):
Applying Table/Column/Row-Level Security (RLS) only at the SQL Endpoint
leaves the underlying Delta files accessible via Spark notebooks or OneLake
APIs. Users with workspace Contributor roles bypass all SQL filters completely.
1. Secure the Write / Storage Path: Use OneLake security roles and workspace
Viewer roles to lock down raw underlying file system access.
2. Secure the Read Path: Apply T-SQL granular permissions for SQL consumers.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Medallion Architecture Diagram, August 2026. Sourced from Microsoft Learn: Lakehouse Overview & SQL Analytics Endpoint Architecture.
